summary: Shows registering multiple variables via register projections (command_result, start/end times, duration) and explains expressions must not use {{ }}; projections can reference each other in any order.
questions: How do I register a command's duration as a variable?
Should I use curly braces in register projections?
Can register projection variables reference each other?

answer_card.title: Register projections
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.shell: /usr/bin/foo
  register:
    command_result: _task.result
    command_start: _task.result.start | to_datetime(time_format)
    command_end: _task.result.end | to_datetime(time_format)
    command_duration: (command_end - command_start).total_seconds()
  vars:
    time_format: '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f'
```

These are always Jinja expressions, so **don't** use `{{ }}` (write `foo: _task.result`). Variables in the same map can reference each other in any order.
